option.counterfactual: There exists a finite AW*-factor satisfying the problem's hypotheses that contains a sequence meeting all the conditions for some positive increment.
option.approach: Study how a single witness can be transformed by corners, matrix amplification, scaling, and quasitracial ultraproducts. Determine whether these operations force the supremum of the possible increments to equal one half.

judge.reason: It claims an exact value for the set, identical to the answer in e3.

options.counterfactual: No finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace admits the sequence required in the problem, so the set of possible increments is empty.
options.approach: Audit the claimed existence of a witness and distinguish it from the existence of a bounded increasing sequence with positive quasitrace gaps. The latter does not automatically satisfy the additional requirement of having no least upper bound.

options.counterfactual: Positive increments are possible, but their supremum is strictly less than one half; corners and matrix amplification cannot always increase an existing increment toward one half.
options.approach: Define the maximal increment and derive necessary inequalities for the spectral distribution of an extremal sequence. Search for an operator-level restriction that selects a value below one half rather than relying only on scalar convexity.

options.counterfactual: Even when positive increments exist, their supremum need not be attained: the quasitracial ultraproduct argument can fail to preserve the absence of a least upper bound.
options.approach: Audit the countable-saturation argument, especially whether order inequalities and quasitrace lower bounds are expressible by uniformly continuous conditions in the quasitrace metric. Identify any condition for which finite satisfiability does not justify realization.
